method PowerOfListElements(l: seq<int>, n: int) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires n >= 0
    ensures |result| == |l|
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |l| ==> result[i] == Power(l[i], n)

    result := [];

        invariant forall k :: 0 <= k < (i) - 1 ==> result[k] == Power(l[k], n)
    {
        result := result + [Power(l[i], n)];
    }
}

function Power(base: int, exponent: int): int
    requires exponent >= 0
{
    if exponent == 0 then 1
    else base * Power(base, exponent-1)

reasoning_content:
I'm tracing the line numbers in the loop to identify that the forall invariant on line 10 is the one failing to be maintained, and considering why its bound might be too weak.

Right, the gap is k = i-1: the old bound only guarantees properties for k < i-1, but the new element being appended sits at index i, so the loop body doesn't justify extending the guarantee up through i-1. That's the preservation failure, and it also explains the postcondition failure at the end. The fix is widening the bound to k < i.
